I. GENERAL

The National Objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as stipulated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph, include: (1) Protecting the entire Indonesian nation and all Indonesian territory, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) educating the life of the nation and (4) participating in the implementation of world order based on (a) independence, (b) permanent peace, and (c) social justice. To achieve these objectives, in accordance with the doctrine of trias politica, there are three powers of the State namely the Executive, Legislative, and Judiciary. In Indonesia these three powers complement each other, for the implementation of a clean and authoritative government from the national level to the regional level.

The Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a State of power (machtstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of power, carried out by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, however in reality there are still many women and children who become victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation below it.

The regional autonomy that is implemented has strategic value so that each region forms legislation (regional regulations), not only to express local wisdom, but also to serve as a guide for regional governments to implement the legislation above it (the 1945 Constitution, and other Laws) to address legal problems and social problems that occur specifically in each region.

This Regional Regulation on the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is based on Pancasila, and based on the 1945 Constitution, and refers to many Laws, especially those governing the protection of women and children victims of violence, including Law No. 7 of 1984 on Ratification of the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, Law No. 39 of 1999 on Human Rights, Law No. 23 of 2004 on the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law No. 35 of 2014 on the Amendment of Law No. 23 of 2002 on Child Protection, and other related Laws.

With the provisions of the above Laws, we can understand how great the attention of the Central Government is to protect its citizens who are in an unpleasant position, namely when they become victims of violence, however in reality legal processes are still rarely carried out for victims of violence which nowadays are increasingly numerous and complex in their problems. And in South Bangka very few existing problems can be resolved legally due to ignorance of the community and the absence of specific legal regulations that become legal regulations that can be used in the region.

It is hoped that with the enactment of this Regional Regulation on the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, particularly in South Bangka Regency, the handling and rehabilitation as well as reunification can be carried out properly, and the process of preventing violence against women and children becomes smoother, so that there will be fewer and eventually no more violence against women and children.

c. carrying out community empowerment for the prevention of violence.

(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be organized according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 2

The implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principle of respect and recognition of human rights and dignity.

Article 10

(1) The Regional Government has the duty to carry out efforts to prevent, handle and recover victims of violence against Women and Children, by:

a. collecting data and information about Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. conducting socialization of Laws and Regulations related to the protection of women and children victims of violence; c. conducting education on anti-violence values against children and women; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection of Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Regional Government is obliged to carry out efforts to prevent, handle and recover victims of violence against women and children, provide and organize services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the formation of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements; b. encouraging public awareness of the importance of protection for victims; and
c. carrying out community empowerment for the prevention of violence.

Article 11

(1) The Regional Government in the implementation of protection of Victims of Violence by involving community participation.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out in the form of:

a. preventing acts of violence against women and children; b.submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against women and children occur; and

I. GENERAL

The National Objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as stipulated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph, include: (1) Protecting the entire Indonesian nation and all Indonesian territory, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) educating the life of the nation and (4) participating in the implementation of world order based on (a) independence, (b) permanent peace, and (c) social justice. To achieve these objectives, in accordance with the doctrine of trias politica, there are three powers of the State namely the Executive, Legislative, and Judiciary. In Indonesia these three powers complement each other, for the implementation of a clean and authoritative government from the national level to the regional level.

The Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a State of power (machtstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of power, carried out by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, however in reality there are still many women and children who become victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation below it.

The regional autonomy that is implemented has strategic value so that each region forms legislation (regional regulations), not only to express local wisdom, but also to serve as a guide for regional governments to implement the legislation above it (the 1945 Constitution, and other Laws) to address legal problems and social problems that occur specifically in each region.

This Regional Regulation on the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is based on Pancasila, and based on the 1945 Constitution, and refers to many Laws, especially those governing the protection of women and children victims of violence, including Law No. 7 of 1984 on Ratification of the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, Law No. 39 of 1999 on Human Rights, Law No. 23 of 2004 on the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law No. 35 of 2014 on the Amendment of Law No. 23 of 2002 on Child Protection, and other related Laws.

With the provisions of the above Laws, we can understand how great the attention of the Central Government is to protect its citizens who are in an unpleasant position, namely when they become victims of violence, however in reality legal processes are still rarely carried out for victims of violence which nowadays are increasingly numerous and complex in their problems. And in South Bangka very few existing problems can be resolved legally due to ignorance of the community and the absence of specific legal regulations that become legal regulations that can be used in the region.

It is hoped that with the enactment of this Regional Regulation on the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, particularly in South Bangka Regency, the handling and rehabilitation as well as reunification can be carried out properly, and the process of preventing violence against women and children becomes smoother, so that there will be fewer and eventually no more violence against women and children.

8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb.

Violence against women is any act based on gender difference that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.

21. Information is a message (utterance or expression) or collection of messages consisting of an ordered sequence of symbols, or meaning that can be interpreted from the message or collection of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.

The Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a State of power (machtstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of power, carried out by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, however in reality there are still many women and children who become victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation below it.

The regional autonomy that is implemented has strategic value so that each region forms legislation (regional regulations), not only to express local wisdom, but also to serve as a guide for regional governments to implement the legislation above it (the 1945 Constitution, and other Laws) to address legal problems and social problems that occur specifically in each region.

This Regional Regulation on the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is based on Pancasila, and based on the 1945 Constitution, and refers to many Laws, especially those governing the protection of women and children victims of violence, including Law No. 7 of 1984 on Ratification of the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, Law No. 39 of 1999 on Human Rights, Law No. 23 of 2004 on the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law No. 35 of 2014 on the Amendment of Law No. 23 of 2002 on Child Protection, and other related Laws.

With the provisions of the above Laws, we can understand how great the attention of the Central Government is to protect its citizens who are in an unpleasant position, namely when they become victims of violence, however in reality legal processes are still rarely carried out for victims of violence which nowadays are increasingly numerous and complex in their problems. And in South Bangka very few existing problems can be resolved legally due to ignorance of the community and the absence of specific legal regulations that become legal regulations that can be used in the region.

It is hoped that with the enactment of this Regional Regulation on the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, particularly in South Bangka Regency, the handling and rehabilitation as well as reunification can be carried out properly, and the process of preventing violence against women and children becomes smoother, so that there will be fewer and eventually no more violence against women and children.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is South Bangka Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of South Bangka.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Council of South Bangka Regency as an element of regional government administration.
5. Principle of Respect and Recognition of Human Rights and Dignity is based on Respect for the rights of victims, Justice and gender equality, Non-Discrimination and the best interests of victims.
6. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence, hospital-based, jointly managed in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psychological and legal services.
7. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb.
9. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or distress whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
11. Violence against women is any act based on gender difference that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
12. Violence against children is any act that results in suffering or distress to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty.
13. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.
14. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.
15. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance.
16. Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
17. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 18. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear or have experienced violence against women. 19. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
20. Optimal service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best goal.
21. Information is a message (utterance or expression) or collection of messages consisting of an ordered sequence of symbols, or meaning that can be interpreted from the message or collection of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the Region to the Region of Origin.

CHAPTER III

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 10

(1) The Regional Government has the duty to carry out efforts to prevent, handle and recover victims of violence against Women and Children, by:

a. collecting data and information about Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. conducting socialization of Laws and Regulations related to the protection of women and children victims of violence; c. conducting education on anti-violence values against children and women; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection of Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Regional Government is obliged to carry out efforts to prevent, handle and recover victims of violence against women and children, provide and organize services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the formation of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements; b. encouraging public awareness of the importance of protection for victims; and
c. carrying out community empowerment for the prevention of violence.

Article 15

(1) Every victim of violence has the right to receive protection in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

(2) Protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to residents of South Bangka Regency whether committed in the territory of South Bangka Regency or outside the territory of South Bangka Regency.

(3) In addition to protection for victims who are residents of South Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), protection shall also be provided to non-residents of South Bangka for incidents committed or occurring in the territory of South Bangka Regency.

Article 16

(1) Forms of protection provided to Victims organized by P2TP2A include protection:

a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medico-legal (forensic medicine);
d. psychological; or
e. economic.
(2) Form of medical protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the victim's physical condition.
(3) Form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) Form of medico-legal protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for purposes of legal evidence.
(5) Form of psychological protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide psychological support so that victims have confidence, strength and independence in solving problems.
(5) Form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

Article 6

Service and Assistance is an activity carried out to serve, protect victims of violence against women and children from the beginning of reporting to the legal process and psychological recovery until the repatriation process.
